Where to Stay in Trang?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Trang hotels across every budget — from beachfront villas on Koh Mook and Koh Kradan to an old-town boutique and a central dorm from ฿470/night. Covering the main areas: Koh Mook, Koh Kradan, Pak Meng and Trang Town. From roughly ฿470–3,500/night.
heroStats: 🏝️ 4 key areas (Koh Mook·Koh Kradan·Pak Meng·Trang Town)
introH2: 🏝️ Why does choosing the right area in Trang matter so much?
introHtml: Trang has both islands and a town, and each area has a completely different vibe. Koh Mook is famous for the Emerald Cave and a clear-water sandspit beach — calm and quiet, a 30–45 min boat from Kuan Tung Ku or Pak Meng pier. Koh Kradan is a white-sand island many people call the prettiest in Trang, ideal for sleeping right on the beach, though stays are few and simple. Pak Meng is a mainland beach near the island piers, handy for a night before an early boat. And Trang Town (Thap Thiang) is the old-town heart — Sino-Portuguese shophouses, morning dim sum and night markets, easy to get around and cheap, perfect as a base before heading to the islands. Many people book without checking whether their stay is on an island or in town, then lose time shuttling back and forth by boat. This guide rounds up 11 Trang hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Trang has no metro, but there's a central railway station (Southern Line to Trang) and Trang Airport (TST) about 15 min from town. The key thing is that island stays need a boat — Koh Mook is a 30–45 min boat from Kuan Tung Ku or Pak Meng pier; Koh Kradan is roughly 45–60 min from Pak Meng or Kuan Tung Ku (some boats don't run in monsoon season). Pak Meng beach is in Sikao district, about a 40 min drive from town. In town you can walk the old quarter and grab a taxi or rent a scooter easily. The areas in this guide: Koh Mook — Emerald Cave, sandspit beach, clear water · Koh Kradan — Trang's prettiest white-sand beach · Pak Meng — mainland beach near the island piers · Trang Town — old town, dim sum, night markets, easiest access.

entries.name: Koh Mook Sivalai Beach Resort
entries.badge: 🏆 Highest score · beachfront on Koh Mook
tags: 🏖️ Set on a sandspit with beach on both sides
🐠 Near the Emerald Cave and snorkel spots
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.4 — Sivalai is a beachfront resort on Koh Mook set right on a sandspit, with beach on both sides, a rare feature that lets you watch both sunrise and sunset in one place. Villas are beachfront and garden, each with a private terrace, ideal for couples and quiet getaways. Real guest reviews praise the sandspit location and sea views, but note Koh Mook needs a boat and dining outside the resort is limited. Best for those who want to genuinely sleep on an island beach near the Emerald Cave.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entry-level Deluxe Villa is already lovely; move up to a Beachfront Villa only if you want to step straight onto the sand from your terrace. Take the boat from Kuan Tung Ku or Pak Meng and check schedules ahead — some boats don't run in monsoon season.
pros: Highest score in the guide 9.4 — consistent on Booking and Agoda
On a sandspit with beach on both sides — sunrise and sunset
Private beachfront villas with sea-view terraces
Near the Emerald Cave and Koh Mook snorkel spots
cons: Koh Mook needs a boat; dining outside the resort is limited
Boats to the island can be cancelled in monsoon season

entries.name: GinGin Hotel, Trang Old Town
tags: 🍜 Walk to dim sum and night markets
🛏️ Has corner rooms and a Suite
entries.addr: 23 Rama VI Rd, Thap Thiang, Mueang Trang, Trang
entries.storyHtml: GinGin is the top-scoring in-town stay in this guide at 9.0, a boutique hotel inside a restored old-town building. The draw is the conversion of an old shophouse into modern design rooms, in a spot where you can walk to morning dim sum and the night markets. Real guest reviews praise the design and old-town location, but honestly there aren't many reviews yet (15) since it's fairly new. Best for those who love old-town character and want a stylish room in the heart of Thap Thiang.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a wider room with light from two sides, pick a Corner room. Get up early to eat at a famous old-town dim sum shop — it's a Trang signature.
pros: Score 9.0 — highest among in-town stays
Restored old shophouse turned boutique design rooms
Old-town location, walk to dim sum and night markets

entries.name: Ban Aothong Hotel

entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Trang · near the train station
entries.addr: 25/28-31 Sathani Rd, Thap Thiang, Mueang Trang, Trang
entries.storyHtml: Ban Aothong has the most reviews in this guide — over 820, with a score of 8.6, a number that tells you it's a stay people pick again and again. The draw is a Thai Lanna style in the city centre, near Trang railway station, with rates from just ฿600 and Family rooms for groups. Real guest reviews praise the value and location, but warn that the cheapest Standard rooms are ground-floor with no window, so it's worth moving up to one with a window. Best for budget travellers who want a dependable stay in the centre.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The cheapest Standard is ground-floor with no window; for a little natural light, choose one with a window. Travelling as a group? The Family Room splits cheaper per person.
pros: Most reviews in the guide 820 — solid, trustworthy data
From ฿600 in the city centre — great value

tags: 🏙️ High-rise in the heart of town

entries.addr: 69/8 Huai Yot Rd, Thap Thiang, Mueang Trang, Trang
entries.storyHtml: Thumrin Thana is a 4-star high-rise in the heart of Trang Town, a long-standing landmark of the city, scoring 8.4 from 68 reviews. The draw is spacious rooms and full facilities including on-site dining and common areas, working for both families and work trips. Real guest reviews praise the room size and central location, but note it's a hotel that's been open a while and some areas show their age, so it's worth picking a renovated room. Best for those who want a full-service hotel in Trang Town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a newer room with city views, move up to a Premier Deluxe on a higher floor. The central location makes it easy to grab a ride to the old town and railway station.
pros: Full-service 4-star hotel in the heart of Trang Town
Spacious rooms, with bathtub options and a Junior Suite
Full facilities — good for families and work trips

entries.name: A Local Something
entries.mrtTag: 📍 City centre · near station and night market
tags: 🪙 Dorm from ฿470 — cheapest in the guide
🚉 Near the station and night market
entries.addr: 88 Kantang Rd, Thap Thiang, Mueang Trang, Trang
entries.storyHtml: A Local Something is the cheapest stay in this guide, with dorm beds from just ฿470 yet a score as high as 9.2. The draw is a converted shophouse in the city centre, walkable to the railway station and night market, with dorm beds that have reading lights, plugs and personal lockers, plus a female-only dorm and private rooms. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness and location, but it's honest to say reviews are still few (12) and it's a hostel — not for those who want lots of privacy. Best for backpackers and solo travellers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want privacy but still good value? Choose the Private Double Room. The location near the station suits anyone arriving in Trang by train who can walk straight to their stay.

entries.storyHtml: ChomTrang is a budget stay right opposite Trang railway station, from just ฿550 with a score of 8.4 from 90 reviews. Real guest reviews praise the location and cleanliness, but note it's a budget stay with simple rooms for the price. Best for budget travellers and those relying on the train.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Arrive in Trang by morning train and walk straight to your stay — it's that close. To start the day well, pick the breakfast-included room, or walk to a famous dim sum shop in town.

entries.name: Kradan Beach Resort

entries.storyHtml: Kradan Beach Resort is a beachfront bungalow resort on Koh Kradan, the island many call Trang's prettiest white-sand beach, scoring 7.8 from 33 reviews. The draw is the beachfront location and island simplicity, with rooms from budget fan rooms up to beachfront bungalows. Real guest reviews praise the location and beautiful beach, but it's honest to say the rooms and amenities are simple in island style, and a mid-range score places it later in the guide. Best for those set on sleeping on Koh Kradan's beach, not on luxury.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Want to wake to the sea? Choose a Beachfront Bungalow. Koh Kradan is basic — power and signal can be limited at times, so set expectations on amenities, and check boat schedules ahead; some boats don't run in monsoon season.

entries.storyHtml: Pakmeng Resort is a beachfront bungalow resort on Pak Meng Beach, near the island pier and handy for a night before an early boat, scoring 6.8 from 22 reviews. The draw is a mainland location near the Pak Meng pier, with rooms from Superior up to sea-view rooms and waterfront bungalows. Real guest reviews praise the location near the pier, but it's honest to say the overall score is still middling and some rooms show their age, placing it late in the guide. Best for those using Pak Meng as a base before heading to Koh Mook or Koh Kradan.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use it as a stay the night before an early boat to save time. For a sea view, choose a Deluxe Sea View or Bungalow Water Front, and check room condition and boat schedules ahead.

entries.name: Anantara Si Kao Resort & Spa
entries.addr: 198-199 Moo 5, Changlang Beach, Maifad, Sikao, Trang
entries.storyHtml: We've put this at the end for honesty — Anantara Si Kao Resort & Spa has been closed since 2018, after the Supreme Court cancelled its land title for overlapping protected forest and Hat Chao Mai National Park and ordered it removed. While it was open, this was the most talked-about 5-star beachfront resort in Sikao: 138 sea-view rooms, gardens landscaped by Bill Bensley, a Google rating of 4.6/5 from 213 reviews. But you can no longer book a stay, even though several booking sites still list it with current-year rates. We include it as a heads-up, not a recommendation.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you see Anantara Si Kao with a price on a booking site, treat it as a stale listing and don't pay before confirming it's actually open. For a beach feel around Sikao–Pak Meng on a real budget, look at Pakmeng Resort, or sleep by the sea on Koh Mook or Koh Kradan instead.
pros: Was Sikao's most renowned 5-star Andaman resort
Sea-view rooms and service won steady praise (pre-closure)

cons: Closed since 2018 — cannot be booked
Some booking sites still list it, making it look open

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Trang hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in Trang?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style. Koh Mook suits those who want to sleep on an island beach, near the Emerald Cave with clear water (Koh Mook Sivalai). Koh Kradan has the prettiest white sand in Trang, simple and close to nature (Kradan Beach Resort). Pak Meng is a mainland beach near the pier, handy before a boat (Pakmeng Resort). Trang Town (Thap Thiang) is the old town with dim sum, night markets, the easiest access and cheapest rates (GinGin, Thumrin Thana, Ban Aothong, ChomTrang, Namthip, Lamoon, A Local Something, BB Trang).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Trang hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: dorms and budget in-town stays start around ฿470–600 per night; boutiques and mid-range to 4-star city hotels run ฿750–1,500; island beach resorts start around ฿1,800–3,500+. All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms. In High Season (Nov–Apr) prices are higher than usual and rooms fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get to Koh Mook and Koh Kradan?
faq.a: The beachfront stays in this guide are on islands and need a boat. Koh Mook is a 30–45 min boat from Kuan Tung Ku or Pak Meng pier. Koh Kradan is a 45–60 min boat from Pak Meng or Kuan Tung Ku. Pak Meng beach is in Sikao district, about a 40 min drive from Trang Town. In monsoon season (May–Oct) the sea is rough and boats to the islands may not run on some days, so check the weather first.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Trang hotel?
faq.a: On weekdays outside the high season, 2–3 weeks ahead is enough. But in High Season (November–April), especially New Year, Songkran and the Trang Roast Pork Festival, island beach resorts fill very fast, so book a month or more ahead. In monsoon season (May–Oct) prices drop but some island resorts close seasonally, so check before booking.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Trang, and is it open year-round?
faq.a: The best time is November–April, when the sea is calm and clear and the weather is good for island trips. In monsoon season (May–October) the sea is rough, it rains, boats to Koh Mook and Koh Kradan may not run on some days, and some island resorts close seasonally. In-town stays in Trang are open year-round, so a monsoon trip focused on the old town, dim sum and local food is more convenient.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Trang hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) differ by promotion and period, so it's best to compare all three before booking. Each review page in this guide has price-comparison links — that can save several hundred baht a night, especially for island beach resorts in peak season.

faq.q: ❓ Is Anantara Si Kao in Trang still open?
faq.a: No, it's closed. Anantara Si Kao Resort & Spa has been closed since 2018, after the Supreme Court cancelled its land title for overlapping protected forest and Hat Chao Mai National Park and ordered it removed. We include it at the end of this guide as a heads-up, because several booking sites still list the name with current-year prices even though you can no longer stay there. For a beach feel around Sikao–Pak Meng, look at Pakmeng Resort, or sleep by the sea on Koh Mook or Koh Kradan instead.
